title: The Value of Information from Sell-side Analysts

live_model.evidence: "I employ the GPT-4-turbo model to categorize each sentence in a random sample of 100 analyst reports into a single, most relevant topic." Prompt 2 (sentence classification) quoted in full.

prompt.location: Sec 2.2: "Prompt 1" (topic discovery, ChatGPT-4o) and "Prompt 2" (sentence classification into 17 categories, GPT-4-turbo) both quoted verbatim
prompt.note: Both prompts are printed in full, including the JSON-output instruction for Prompt 2.

claim.metric: none validated for GPT-4-turbo itself; downstream fine-tuned BERT classifier reaches 89% accuracy on GPT-4-turbo-labeled data
claim.location: Sec 2.2: BERT test accuracy 89%; "less than 5%" fallback rate for the 16 GPT-generated topics; exact number of GPT-4-turbo-labeled sentences not stated as one figure

data.source: Proprietary sell-side analyst reports (6,975,114 sentences total); not released

notes: Both prompts are fully reproducible text (a real strength), but GPT-4-turbo's own labeling is never checked against independent ground truth -- the paper instead validates the pipeline indirectly via a downstream BERT classifier's accuracy (89%), a low fallback-category rate, and word-cloud coherence, none of which is GPT-4-turbo's own capability score. Undated in text; arXiv id (2411, Nov 2024) places it after the alias cutoffs, so gpt-4-turbo resolves cleanly even though no in-text date string exists.
